account: Today I attended morning office hours and my market walk, then returned home for noon lunch. I have a vague feeling that something is happening without me, but so far I have found no definite evidence of a secret undertaking. Several townspeople had no news; others merely reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. I saw the baker stock bread at the market stall. The baker said thirty-two fresh loaves were stocked, reported no difficulties or confirmed news, and asked whether any town gatherings would need bread. That could simply be ordinary business, not evidence that a gathering is planned. The secretary initially asked which engagements to enter despite my existing appointment schedule, but has now confirmed my three o'clock tea with someone called neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage, at (16, -60, 105). The host's unusual name and the initially unnamed appointment are worth following up, but I do not yet know anything suspicious about the visit or its purpose beyond tea. My next obligations are town accounts at one, tea at three, and office at four-thirty. Visiting the neighbour should give me a natural opportunity to learn more about life and news on the east bank.
